title: Product overview — exploration C
summary: Concept C, guided setup first: while Integration is shown, DJDL's Overview leads with a setup stepper (one step per feature on a rail, platform badges, the first open step expanded with its console step and drop-in kit), attention pinned above it, and the features' facts and recent activity in one compact pair under it.
compare: Concept C, guided setup first. While Integration is shown, the page reads top to bottom: the pinned attention row, the Integration card as the setup stepper, then one compact pair with Features and Recent activity. Once the operator hides Integration, the same page leads with Features (facts first) under the attention row; that state isn't drawn here.

Header: DJDL's logo, name and slug, 'A DJ app for macOS and Windows', and only ⋯ More. No 'Continue integration': the open step on the page is where integration continues, so the header doesn't send people to it a second time.

Attention is pinned above the stepper as one card with a warning border and no visible head (its h2 'Needs attention' is for screen readers): the Warning pill, Managed config, 'Required secret identity.acoustidKey has no value in the Default profile.' and 'Set secret →', in the same words as Home. On phone it stacks: pill and subject, the message, then the link.
Integration head: 'Integration' at the block step and a ghost 'Hide' (eye-off, aria-label 'Hide Integration') on the right, offered because macOS has a Verified feature and never automatic.

The platform band under the head is the one place each platform is summed up: macOS with '2 of 5 verified', its bar and 'Swift SDK 2.1.0 · last seen 4 min ago'; Windows with 'Not seen yet', an empty bar and 'Add the SDK →' (Integration's SDK picker with Windows selected). The words 'Not seen yet' appear once on the page.

The stepper is one row per enabled feature in canonical order (Commerce is off, so no row), joined by a rail: a green tick and a green rail for Licensing and Managed config (verified on macOS, the only platform seen), Ship builds' own accent ring (the first open step), a neutral clock for Sign-in ('Waiting for the first sign-in') and an open ring for Cloud Sync, whose sub-line is the open console step as one verb link, 'Set storage per account'. Done rows carry no sub-line. Ship builds' sub-line is its CI fact, 'First CI publish Oct 6'. Rows are 56px.

Platform badges: each row ends in one 28px tile per platform, its glyph with the Verified state as a corner mark: green tile and tick (Verified; the time is in its label, 'macOS: Verified Oct 7, 10:42'), clock (Waiting), open ring (After the console step), dashed outline with no mark (Not seen yet). They are tiles, not pills, because healthy states never take pill shape; each has role=img and the full state as its accessible name and title.

The open step's work sits beside the list (desktop, wide and tablet) in the same tint as its row, so the row reads as the tab of that pane: 'In the console' with 'Sparkle signing key', 'Run this in the repository, then push.' and the command 'pkey release keys init --sparkle' with Copy; then 'Drop-in kit' with the generated kit code first (Swift · macOS, Kotlin · Windows tabs, Copy) and 'Your own UI ↗' on the same line (aria-label 'Integrate Ship builds directly with your own UI: Swift SDK docs'). The two parts sit side by side when each gets 300px (desktop, wide), else stacked (tablet).

Every row is one button (aria-expanded) that opens its own step in the pane, so each feature leads with its drop-in kit and its 'Your own UI' link one click away (owner, 2026-10-08) without repeating two links on five rows.

Features is a compact card: 'Features' and 'Manage features →', six cells three by two (two by three on a card under 680px, 56px rows under 560px), values at 18/24: Licensing '240 licenses', 'Standard · 3 waiting'; Managed config 'v4 catalog', '12 settings · 3 secrets' with the warning dot (aria-label 'Managed config: 1 needs attention'); Ship builds '4.2.0 stable', '4.3.0-beta.2 on beta · Oct 6'; Sign-in '312 accounts', 'Pocket ID · members, admins'; Cloud Sync 'Not syncing yet'; Commerce 'Off' with a muted glyph (a service that may be off; it links to Features). Each cell links to its feature's home.
Recent activity is the pair's narrow card: three events with the time 4px under the text and 'Open Activity →'. At wide the aside shows two more (Cloud Sync turned on, Tomás Okafor joined as editor).

Desktop (1440) and tablet (1024): Features and Recent activity side by side under the stepper (about 2:1), the Features strip filling its card's height. Tablet keeps the list and pane side by side at 920px (list 380, pane stacked). Wide (1920): the main column holds attention, Integration and Features (three by two at 1184); Recent activity is the 400px aside, the shorter column.

Phone: the stepper becomes an accordion: each row keeps its badges beside the title and gains a chevron; the open step's work drops under its row in the row's tint, reaching the card's edge so the command shows whole. The band stacks macOS over Windows. Features are 56px rows; activity rows stack.
Sidebar as on every DJDL screen: one count, on Devices (412); feature groups as muted labels with their 2px service bar; at tablet the 56px icon rail.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink; focus, hover, checked and selected take the accent of the service the element references (B17), never a status colour; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.
B17: the attention row, each step, feature cell and activity row carries the service it references; the join row is core.

designReview.reviewer: Senior product designer (Concept C, guided setup first)
designReview.verdict: Exploration for the owner to compare with the current Overview: the integration matrix becomes a setup stepper with the open step's work beside it, attention is pinned above, and facts and activity drop to one compact pair. Kit additions are appended to mockup.css under 'Guided setup (products.overview-c)'.
